questions.question: What is the primary advantage of open-source LLMs like Llama 3.1 over closed-source models like GPT-4o?
options: They always produce higher-quality outputs
They can be downloaded, fine-tuned, and deployed on private infrastructure
They have larger context windows
They are always faster at inference
questions.explanation: Open-source models like Llama 3.1 can be self-hosted, giving full control over data privacy and customization. However, they require significant infrastructure investment and are not inherently better in quality.

questions.question: A company processes 50,000 simple classification tasks per day. Which model tier is most cost-effective?
options: GPT-4o for maximum accuracy
Claude 3.5 Sonnet for long-context understanding
GPT-4o mini, Gemini 1.5 Flash, or Claude 3 Haiku
Llama 3.1 70B self-hosted
questions.explanation: For high-volume simple tasks like classification, small/cheap models (GPT-4o mini, Flash, Haiku) deliver sufficient quality at a fraction of the cost. Self-hosting 70B would be more expensive at this scale given infrastructure overhead.

questions.question: What does the 'lost in the middle' phenomenon refer to in LLMs?
options: Models forget their system prompt after long conversations
Models perform worse on information placed in the middle of very long contexts
Models lose accuracy when processing multiple languages
Models cannot retrieve embeddings from middle-indexed vector stores
questions.explanation: Research shows LLMs attend more strongly to information at the beginning and end of their context window, while information buried in the middle is more likely to be missed — even in models with very large context windows like Gemini's 1M tokens.

questions.question: What does RLHF stand for and why is it important for LLM selection?
options: Recursive Language Hyperparameter Fitting — it optimizes training speed
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback — it makes models more helpful and aligned
Randomized Layer Hierarchical Fusion — it improves model architecture
Real-time Language Hallucination Fixing — it reduces incorrect outputs
questions.explanation: RLHF fine-tunes models based on human preference labels to be more helpful, harmless, and honest. A well-aligned smaller model can outperform an unaligned larger model on real-world tasks, making alignment quality a critical selection criterion.

questions.question: When is self-hosting open-source LLMs typically MORE expensive than using API-based models?
options: When processing more than 1 million tokens per day
When monthly API costs would be under ~$500/month
When data privacy is a concern
When using quantized models
questions.explanation: Running a 70B model in production requires GPU hardware ($10K-15K/month), engineering time, and maintenance. Below ~$500/month in API costs, the infrastructure and engineering overhead of self-hosting makes it more expensive than simply paying for API access.
